0.2 Moulds and cores with high degree of dimensional accuracy are commonly made by using `No Bake Binder' mixed with sand. Increased productivity and excellent breakdown properties are considered to be additional advantages. 0.2.1 The binder base, furan base, and accelerator:). for c. between the is a proprietory resin of one of the following types:

a) Phenol b) Urea

c) Alkyd base ( with or without 0.2.1.1 The hardener

is an acid for a, b and isocyanate reaction

0.2.2 The hardening binder and the catalyst

is effected by a chemical without any external heat.

0.3 Proper choice of the system is necessary for successful production different types of castings, such as steel, cast iron and non-ferrous.

of

0.3.1 Type (b) are not suitable for steel castings whereas most of the ferrous and non-ferrous castings may be produced from (a), (b) and (c) types of resins. 0.3.2 On curing, the phenolic system turns to pink, the furan system turns to green and the alkyd system does not change from the original colour of the sand. 0.3.3 Basically for safe handling phenolic system is toxic in nature. NOTE - The use of the ISI Certification Mark is governed by the provisions of the Indian Standards Institution (Certification Marks) Act and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The ISI Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the testing requirements of that standard under a well-defined system of inspection, and quality control which is devised and supervised by IS1 and operated by the producer. ISI marked products are also continuously checked by IS1 for conformity Details of conditions under which a to that standard as a further safeguard. licence for the use of the IS1 Certification Mark may be granted to manufacturers or processors, may be obtained from the Indian Standards Institution.

the standard

A-4.1 Weighed quantity of sand shall be charged in the dry and clean mixer. Weighed quantity of catalyst shall be added uniformly on the sand bed while the mixture is on. Sand and the catalyst together shall be mixed for two minutes. Then the binder shall be added as before and mixed for three minutes and discharged into a clean bucket. A-5. TESTING PROCEDURE numbers very quickly of 50 x 50 mm from the mix, using

A-5.1 Test for Bench Life-Eight standard sand sample shall be prepared 7

IS : 10032- 1981
split specimen tube and tested at an interval of 5 minutes for compression strength. The stripping of the sand specimen shall be done just prior to testing. O*OlO MPa green strength indicates the end of bench life. A-5.2 Development of Strength on Core - Immediately after the discharge of sand from the mixer the core box as specified in A-2.4 has to be filled up. During filling, gentle tapping of the sides are necessary to have uniform packing. The top surface of the core shall be levelled off by a metal strip. 5 numbers of vent holes of 6 to 8 mm dia (uniformly spaced) shall be pierced on the top surface. The holes shall be up to about At an interval of every thirty 25 mm above the bottom of the core. minutes after filling the box, strength is required to be tested on the top surface by mould strength tester and recorded. The time to attain The core box shall then be 0.207 MPa indicates the stripping time. opened to observe strength at the side 25 mm from top and bottom and at the middle of the core. The core shall also be examined for sagging tendency by bulging of the sides or collapse. A-5.3 Other tests shall be carried out as per standard adopted in foundry sand testing (see IS : 1918-1966*) testing procedure
